extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in fluid mechanics applying machine learning (including control and optimization specialists)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for using machine learning methods (modeling, optimization, and control) in fluid mechanics research and applications, including algorithm selection, data considerations, reproducibility, and physical consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid learning algorithms when adjoint/gradient methods apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning algorithms are iterative and often require several orders of magnitude more cost function evaluations than gradient based algorithms. They do not offer guarantees of convergence and we suggest that they are avoided when techniques such as adjoint methods are applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer gradient-based/adjoing methods when available and computationally feasible; reserve learning-based approaches for problems where gradient/adjoint methods cannot be applied (e.g., black-box or multimodal cost functions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use surrogate models for optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Machine learning can be applied to develop explicit surrogate models that relate the cost function and the control/optimization parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surrogate models (e.g., neural networks) can be amenable to gradient-based optimization but may get stuck in local minima. Multi-fidelity algorithms can combine surrogates with the full cost function; as learning progresses, new data should be requested guided by optimization results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit high-dimensional/non-convex optimization capabilities of ML
rubrics_metrics.description: The high-dimensional and non-convex optimization procedures currently employed to train nonlinear learning machines are well-suited to the high-dimensional, nonlinear optimization problems in flow control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that training such machines inherits the same challenges (local minima, scaling) and may require substantial computational resources and algorithmic care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer stochastic optimization for black-box and uncertain problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Stochastic optimization (evolutionary strategies, genetic algorithms) is widely used for engineering design, particularly for black-box cost functions and problems with unexpected behavior or partial system descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These algorithms involve many iterations and benefit from massively parallel architectures and automation (including experimental setups). They are suitable when robustness to uncertainty and disturbances is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider convergence proofs, explainability, and reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Convergence proofs, explainability, and reliability are outstanding issues that need to be taken into consideration when deploying stochastic optimization or learning algorithms in fluid mechanics problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the algorithm provides theoretical guarantees or adequate empirical evidence for convergence and robustness before deployment in critical systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use hybrid algorithms when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Hybrid algorithms, combining in a problem-specific manner stochastic techniques and gradient-based methods may offer the best strategy for flow control problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design hybrids to exploit strengths of different approaches (exploration of stochastic methods, efficiency of gradients) and to mitigate weaknesses (convergence, local minima).

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for blurred boundary between optimization and control
rubrics_metrics.description: The distinction between optimization and control is largely semantic and implementation-dependent; solving optimization problems fast enough on the fly can produce feedback control laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When embedding optimization in feedback control, classical control issues (robustness to model uncertainty, time delays, process and measurement noise) become paramount—especially for high-performance aerospace systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design feedback control informed by sensors to handle instability and disturbances
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback flow control modifies fluid behavior through actuation informed by sensor measurements; feedback is necessary to stabilize unstable systems, attenuate sensor noise, and compensate for disturbances and model uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize challenges such as high-dimensional states, nonlinearity, latent variables, and time delays; integrate system identification and sensor-placement strategies into control design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be mindful of neural networks’ parameter/resource demands for control
rubrics_metrics.description: Neural networks offer the ability to approximate arbitrary nonlinear control laws but require many parameters to be optimized and may demand exorbitant computational or experimental resources for complex, high-dimensional configurations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh resource requirements versus potential control performance; note that training times have improved, but careful architecture and training choices remain critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genetic algorithms require pre-specified control-law structure and few parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Genetic algorithms require that the structure of the control law is pre-specified and contains only a few adjustable parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They scale poorly as the number of parameters grows (or with nonlinear/stateful controllers); genetic programming has been successfully used for some active control tasks, often with relatively few test evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design reinforcement learning (RL) with domain knowledge: states, actions, rewards
rubrics_metrics.description: Fluid mechanics knowledge is essential for RL applications because success hinges on properly selecting states, actions, and rewards that reflect governing mechanisms of the flow problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use natural sensors/organisms as inspiration for state choices; actions must reflect actuation devices; rewards should encode relevant performance metrics (e.g., energetic costs, positional objectives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Address computational cost and use parallelism in RL
rubrics_metrics.description: The computational cost of RL remains a challenge to its widespread adoption, but this can be mediated by the parallelism inherent to RL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue methods that enable transfer from low-accuracy to high-accuracy simulations and from simulation to real-world (sim-to-real) to reduce cost and improve applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-validate to avoid overfitting
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important to cross-validate machine learned models, otherwise results may be prone to overfitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt rigorous validation and testing protocols, hold-out datasets, and metrics appropriate to the task (interpolation vs extrapolation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer physics-informed and physics-consistent models
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and adapt machine learning algorithms that are not only physics informed but also physics consistent—a major outstanding challenge in AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed conservation laws, symmetries, invariances, and other known physics either via constraints, architectures, or hybrid modeling approaches to improve generalization and interpretability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider data quality/quantity, inputs/outputs, cost function, and extrapolation needs when choosing methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider several factors when choosing methods, including the quality and quantity of data, the desired inputs and outputs, the cost function to be optimized, whether the task involves interpolation or extrapolation, and how important it is for models to be explainable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match method complexity to available data and problem requirements; explicitly decide if extrapolation is required and choose algorithms accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize reproducibility: document procedures, archive code and data
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproducibility is a cornerstone of science: document procedures, archive code, and host data so that others can reproduce results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create and curate benchmark datasets and software, provide code/data repositories, and follow community standards for reproducible computational science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize fluids data is multimodal and multi-fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: Fluids data is multi-modal and multi-fidelity; it has high-resolution in some dimensions and is sparse in others; many tasks balance multiple objectives; and data comes from a dynamical system where many tasks do not admit post-mortem analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design datasets, benchmarks, and algorithms that explicitly address multi-modality, fidelity gaps, sparsity, multi-objective tradeoffs, and dynamic/online evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for models that are explainable, generalizable, and have guarantees
rubrics_metrics.description: Although many fields focus on raw predictive performance, applications in fluid mechanics often require models that are explainable, generalizable, and have guarantees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize interpretability and theoretical/empirical guarantees where needed for scientific insight or safety-critical applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulate the problem and select data/models carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Properly formulating the question, selecting the data as well as the learning machine and its training is a process where all parts are critical; an algorithm will always provide some kind of answer based on its training data which may not be relevant to the question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest time in problem statement, preprocessing, feature/state selection, and aligning training objectives with the true scientific/engineering goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop benchmark datasets, open standards, and community sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Machine learning encourages open sharing of data and software; creating and curating benchmark datasets and software will spur interest and drive progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support open and reproducible research products and standards tailored for fluid mechanics' specific challenges (multi-fidelity, dynamical data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize sensor placement as an algorithmic and experimental challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimal sensor placement is an algorithmic challenge as sensor technologies progress; sensor placement affects state estimation, control, and RL performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use data-driven sparse sensor placement methods, consider estimation/identification needs, and integrate sensor design with learning/control strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for experimental/industrial constraints when deploying ML
rubrics_metrics.description: Stochastic optimization and learning methods have been facilitated by advances in automation and are used in experimental and industrial settings; they can handle unexpected system behavior and partial descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When deploying in experiments or industry, consider automation, parallel hardware, measurement noise, real-time constraints, and robustness to exogenous disturbances.
